name: Mount Helen and Mount Sacagawea

legs.connect: Drop off Helen by a south-facing couloir just east of the summit, contour across the cirque of the Sacagawea Glacier (narrow snow ramp around the crevassed arm), and gain the gentler east side of Sacagawea.

duration: 1 long day from a Titcomb Basin camp
how: Both summits sit on the Divide above the upper basin and are usually done together from a camp in Titcomb. Helen goes first by its long east ridge, which is mostly scrambling with a short class 4 finish. The link crosses a glacier cirque, so an ice axe is carried and crevasses must be avoided; rockfall below the north gully is a known hazard. Sacagawea's summit ridge is the harder part: class 4 with false summits and heavy exposure. Some parties climb them in the other order.
descent: Sacagawea is left by a talus or scree chute back down into Titcomb Basin, which is quicker than retracing the glacier crossing.
logistics: Long approach from Elkhart Park; camp in upper Titcomb Basin. Snow lingers on the Divide and in the gullies into late summer, so conditions decide how much ice and snow the day holds.
notes: Three independent trip reports climb both (two go Helen then Sacagawea, one Fremont-Sacagawea-Helen). Sacagawea route name not given by sources. Fremont, Jackson, Spearhead and Warren are often added on longer days. Fremont+Jackson from Indian Basin considered and left out: only one site's guide plus one report from the same site were readable.

name: Pollock Mountain and Bishop's Cap

legs.route: The Cleft (narrow gully to near the summit)

legs.connect: Follow the ridge north from Pollock's summit and drop to the saddle between the two, then follow cairns up the cap; helmets at its base.

how: Both are climbed in a single loop from the Lunch Creek parking area. Cliffs south of Pollock lead to the saddle with Piegan Mountain, then the route crosses the face to a gully that nearly reaches the top; falling rock makes a helmet worthwhile. From the summit a cairned trail drops to the next saddle and the cap, which has third and fourth class moves in short sections. One party roped up for both climbs but felt it was not really needed. Piegan Mountain is sometimes added first.
descent: Return to the saddle below the cap and descend its lowest point by a scree field to the Highline Trail, then walk it back to Logan Pass and Lunch Creek.
logistics: Parking fills early in summer, so start before 8 am. Expect roughly 8 miles and about 4,000 to 4,300 feet of gain, around 11 hours for the longer version.
notes: Only two pages read in full; the summit-sharing site returned 403. Class on Pollock not stated. Route names beyond The Cleft not given.

name: Hollowtop Mountain and Mount Jefferson

legs.connect: Walk the short ridge over to Jefferson, a bit under a mile away.

how: Hollowtop, the range high point, is climbed by its steep west side; its neighbour Jefferson is a short walk away and is routinely tagged on the way down. Jefferson's summit is jumbled rock with loose footing and a small cliff band. The pair can also be done as part of a longer ridge loop that crosses Horse Mountain, then a narrow granite ridge over Jefferson and a long boulder ramp to Hollowtop.
descent: After Jefferson, drop back toward the basin below; the loop version instead retraces the ramp and descends the drainage past several lakes to Hollowtop Lake.
logistics: Trailheads are reached by dirt roads past the town of Pony or via the west approach; snow-free season is summer into early fall. Around 2,500 to 3,700 feet of gain depending on the approach.
notes: No class rating in any source. Trailhead names not given; gain differs by route (about 2,500 to Hollowtop Lake only; about 3,700 for the west approach).
